# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503 Incident

**Status at handoff:** UNRESOLVED. Log ends 03:59:27Z with errors still firing and the wait queue still climbing. No recovery observed.

## Root cause

Gateway config change `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true` exhausted the gateway's upstream connection pool. Each request now holds its own connection instead of sharing, so the 20-slot pool pins at full and requests queue until they time out as 503.

```
02:13:41.234Z INFO config generation 119 applied: 3 keys changed
02:13:41.234Z INFO config   gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true
02:13:41.234Z INFO config   gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500
```

Pool went from `in_use=10 idle=10 waiting=0` (02:10) to `in_use=20 idle=0` and never released. The `upstreamMs` 2000→2500 bump in the same change makes each held connection worse.

Every one of the 530 failures carries the same single error code — there is no other error type in the file:

```
ERROR access req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
ERROR pool   req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

**Upstreams are healthy** — all 180 `/health` checks returned 200 across all four services throughout. Do not chase billing/catalog/orders/accounts.

## Impact window

| | |
|---|---|
| First 503 | 2026-03-14 **02:14:18.972Z** (`req-07401`) |
| Last seen | 2026-03-14 **03:59:27.974Z** (`req-17907`) — log ends, still failing |
| Duration | ≥ 1h 45m, ongoing |
| Volume | 530 × 503, steady ~50 per 10 min |
| Blast radius | All routes: `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/profile`. Checkout affected — assume revenue impact. |

## Roll back

**`dep-4471`** — gateway, 02:12:00Z → 02:14:00Z, author **a.novak**, *"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation."*

Revert to **config generation 118**. Deploy finished 02:14:00Z; first 503 landed 18 seconds later.

Ruled out: dep-4472 (billing, 02:41) and dep-4473 (catalog, 03:20) both land after failures were already steady, and errors are spread evenly across all four upstreams rather than concentrated on either.

## Open items for the next shift

1. **Log covers `node-3 of 3` only.** Assume nodes 1 and 2 are equally affected — confirm and roll back fleet-wide, not just this node.
2. **Unexplained queue reset at 03:15** — waiting dropped 232 → 12, then resumed climbing at the same rate. Likely an unlogged restart or eviction; it clears waiters without fixing the leak, so don't read a dip in graphs as recovery.
3. **Separate worker issue, not part of this incident.** `logs/worker.log` shows zero errors but job duration ramping linearly +110ms/10min (327ms → 2197ms). It starts at 01:00 — before dep-4471 — with no inflection at 02:14, and the worker pool is idle (`in_use=1` of 8) with flat 5ms `db_wait`. Possibly dep-4470 (worker, finished 00:55). **Needs its own ticket** and worker logs from before 01:00 to confirm.
4. `WARN db slow query 1.9s ... OPS-2210` at 02:36 in worker.log is a known pre-existing issue, single occurrence, unrelated.

⚠️ **Timeline check before you page anyone:** these logs are dated **2026-03-14**, roughly five months before today (2026-08-27) — not last night. If you're responding to a live incident right now, this file is not it and the current logs need to be located.
